title: Why You Forget Why You Walked Into a Room

scenes.text: Your brain wipes part of your memory every time you walk through a doorway.
Scientists call it the doorway effect.
In experiments, people forgot what they were carrying far more often after passing through a door than after walking the same distance inside one room.
Your brain treats a doorway as the end of one event and the start of a new one, so it files the old details away.
That's why you end up in the kitchen with no idea what you wanted.
The fix? Decide what you need before you walk, and say it out loud.

description: Your brain resets part of its memory every time you walk through a doorway. Psychologists call it the doorway effect. Here's why it happens, and the simple trick to beat it.
